top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's presentation of a painless nodule with well-defined margins, along with immunoreactivity for vimentin and CD34 and negative results for other markers, is most consistent with Solitary Fibrous Tumor.

The characteristics of the lump, including its mobility, painlessness, well-defined margins, and homogeneous echostructure on ultrasound, combined with the fine-needle aspiration results showing only benign duct cells, support Fibroadenoma as a diagnosis.

While Lipoma is a possibility due to the mobile and painless nature of the lump, the presence of benign duct cells in the cytological specimens and the specific immunohistochemical stains suggest it is less likely than Solitary Fibrous Tumor or Fibroadenoma.
The lack of specific findings such as pseudovascular spaces and stromal cell proliferation makes Pseudoangiomatous Stromal Hyperplasia a less likely diagnosis.
The absence of rapid growth, large size, and mitoses, along with the well-defined margins and lack of necrosis or hemorrhage, makes Phyllodes Tumor an unlikely diagnosis.
